articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy criticises Trump for calling Putin his ‘friend’; Kyiv deploys new laser weapon
articles.description: Ukrainian leader likens Putin to Hitler; laser system intercepts Russian drone but not ready for ‘mass deployment’. What we know on day 1,739 Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticised Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin his “friend”, likening the Russian leader to Adolf Hitler. “Of course it’s up to the president of the United States, but ... it’s strange,” the Ukrainian leader told the BBC in an interview aired on Friday. “He is an aggressor, and a killer... He can’t be a friend. Just cannot be. It’s the same that somebody says about Hitler during the second world war, that he’s a good friend. No. He’s not a friend.” Zelenskyy said what was needed was “more progress” and urged Washington to increase pressure on Moscow. Ukraine has for the first time used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered drone, according to its state-backed defence group Brave1. An adviser to Zelenskyy, Serhiy Beskrestnov, published footage earlier this week showing a target crashing in a fireball, saying a Russian Geran jet drone had been shot down by a laser system for the “first time”. Agence France-Presse quoted Brave1 as saying on Friday: “Footage recently emerged online showing a Ukrainian laser system being used in combat to intercept an enemy jet-powered drone.” The weapon was developed by a recipient of a Brave1 grant and operated by a private air defence team, Brave1 added. But it cautioned that “a first successful interception does not mean the technology is ready for mass deployment”. “Laser air defence remains an experimental technology,” it said, adding that at least seven teams in Ukraine were currently working on laser weapons. Beskrestnov said the system, known as Blysk and developed by the Ukrainian company Carmine Sky, was protecting critical infrastructure during the interception. A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles bound for Libya has turned around in the Mediterranean after Ukrainian maritime drones sank a Russian naval warship in Benghazi port last Sunday, Reuters quoted three people from military and security services as saying on Friday. The convoy, which was escorted by the Russian navy frigate Golovko, turned around near the strait of Sicily on the same day as the attack in Benghazi, said a European military official who had been tracking the convoy. A Ukrainian military intelligence official and a Middle East security official confirmed the flotilla had turned from heading to Libya. Russia’s defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Ukraine has offered a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food exports and passed this on to international allies, the foreign minister said. “We are ready for a ceasefire. We are grateful to India, Turkey and Egypt, which are playing an active and important role in de-escalating tensions in the Black Sea, as well as in mediation efforts. We are now awaiting a response from Russia,” Andrii Sybiha was cited by public broadcaster Suspilne as saying on Friday. He added that Russia had proposed Ukraine suspend attacks on the Russian oil sector under the truce, but Kyiv would only consider this as part of a bigger energy ceasefire deal. Ukraine’s military said on Friday it had struck a Russian solid rocket fuel production site in the Tula region south of Moscow overnight. “The plant is the starting point of the missile production chain: it manufactures components for plastic explosives and the polymer used to produce solid propellant for Russian ballistic missiles,” the defence ministry said on Telegram. Russia’s foreign ministry has accused Latvia of creating artificial obstacles to hinder the transit of Russian grain to global markets, saying the restrictions pose additional risks to global food security. Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova claimed in a statement published on the ministry’s website on Friday that Latvia was conducting inspections of Russian grain shipments for allegedly stolen Ukrainian agricultural products and was seeking ways to ban Russian grain transit altogether.
